newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals still mostly lower midday.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals still mostly lower midday.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were off the morning's lows midday Wednesday, but with the exception of silver, were still down on Tuesday's closing levels.
"The open interest data just released for Tuesday suggests you had new shorts in both gold and silver yesterday," Pell Brothers COMEX floor trader Don Tierney said.
COMEX gold open interest jumped 9,775 lots to 197,749 contracts Tuesday, on moderate volume of 48,000 lots as gold prices fell by about $3.50 an ounce.
Midday Tuesday COMEX December gold was down 60 cents at $324.00, but off the morning's lows at $321.50 and Tuesday's three week intraday low at $321.00.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted $319.90/40, compared to the London Wednesday afternoon fix at $319.35 and the New York close Tuesday at $320.20/70.
Implied gold lease rates rose again Wednesday, after falling back from six month highs in the past few weeks as borrowing to fund short positions abated.
One month implied lease rates for gold were around 1.74 pct early Wednesday, up from 1.54 pct Tuesday, after seeing a high around 2.50 pct in early July.
COMEX September silver was up 4.0 cents at $4.355 an ounce, recovering some ground after a sharp 19.2 cent slide Tuesday from three week highs.
COMEX silver open interest rose 2,485 lots Tuesday to 94,293 contracts.

Meanwhile, NYMEX platinum and palladium futures remained sharply lower midday Wednesday, in line with a sharp fall in TOCOM (Tokyo Commodity Exchange) platinum group metal (PGM) futures and in the bullion market overnight.
NYMEX October platinum was down $12.10 an ounce at $437.50, but was well off the morning's lows at $424.60, following a tumble from a contract high at $466.00 Tuesday.
NYMEX September palladium was down $10.60 an ounce at $217.00, after seeing a new contract high at $227.60 Tuesday.
But after a sharp rally in PGMs since mid-July, which took palladium prices back up to new 17 year highs, a correction was not really a surprise, traders said.

In the past week NYMEX and TOCOM PGM futures have seen several days of limit-up moves, driven by fund and broker shortcovering, against a background of an acute shortage of metal in the physical market.
